answer: An agent market weights contract votes by locked collateral, not account count. An attacker can name accounts umber or zenith and create a spiral of aliases, but dividing a $1,000 deposit among them still buys only $1,000 of voting weight. To capture a majority, the attacker must acquire and lock more collateral than all honest voters combined, tying up capital and forgoing its use elsewhere instead of merely generating identities.
